source.authors: Giacinto S. Germinara, Marco Pistillo, Raffaele Griffo, Antonio P. Garonna, Antonella Di Palma
source.title: Electroantennographic Responses of Aromia bungii (Faldermann, 1835) (Coleoptera, Cerambycidae) to a Range of Volatile Compounds

value: male and female antennae gave similar EAG responses to 90 volatile compounds; 17 compounds differed significantly between sexes
method: electroantennography on antennae of males and females, 90 volatile compounds, 1 mg load (10 uL of 100 ug/uL mineral oil solution) per stimulus, mineral oil control and (Z)-3-hexenol standard (10 uL of 10 ug/uL) presented at the start and after each group of five test compounds
conditions: larvae in logs collected from infested apricot trees near Marigliano (Naples, Italy) and reared to adults; 10 to 15 day old unmated adults; each compound tested on five antennae of different insects of each sex, total number of insects not stated; stimuli in random sequence, 1 min apart; a second set used a (Z)-3-hexenol dose series of 0.001 to 100 ug/uL in ascending order on flagellomeres seven to nine; Results: all compounds elicited measurable EAG responses in both sexes (p < 0.05, Wilcoxon rank sum tests), from 0.028 +/- 0.003 mV ((E,E)-2,4-hexadienal) to 1.197 +/- 0.067 mV ((E)-2-hexenol) in males and from 0.019 +/- 0.001 mV (ethyl acetate) to 0.979 +/- 0.057 mV ((E)-2-hexenol) in females; of the 17 differing compounds, male responses exceeded female for 12 and female exceeded male for 5; stimulus amounts are nominal loads, not measured air concentrations
quote: A large degree of similarity between the EAG responses of males and females was observed with only 17 of the 90 compounds tested eliciting significant differences.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page (sentence returned by the page tool in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata gives CC BY 3.0, Crossref gives CC BY 4.0 for the version of record. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from main for sense_chemical (git grep of whole docs tree; only the d217 progress note names the paper as held).

source.authors: Qi Sun, Weicheng Yang, Sheng Liang, Mengqing Zhou, Fen Liu, Xianyu Li, Bibo Zhou, Tianyu Liang
source.title: Electrophysiological and Behavioral Responses of Phthonoloba viridifasciata (Lepidoptera: Geometridae) to Volatiles from Alsophila spinulosa

value: female EAG 0.387 +/- 0.027 mV to 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (largest of the five compounds) and 0.206 +/- 0.008 mV to decane (smallest)
method: electroantennography of adults, five host-fern volatiles in n-hexane, 10 uL on filter paper (10 x 30 mm strip), 0.5 s stimulus, 30 s between stimuli, n-hexane first and last
conditions: larvae collected at the Alsophila National Nature Reserve, Chishui, Guizhou, China and reared separately by sex; adults 2 to 3 days old, unmated; five concentrations (1e-1 to 1e-5 mol/L) applied in ascending order, one stimulation each; the quoted sentence does not say which concentration the mV values come from and the number of antennae is not stated; all five compounds gave EAG responses in both sexes; females were significantly above males for undecane (p < 0.05) and 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (p < 0.01), with no significant sex difference for decane, p-ethylacetophenone and m-ethylacetophenone; stimuli are nominal solution amounts, not measured air concentrations
quote: Female adults exhibited stronger EAG responses to 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (EAG = 0.387 ± 0.027 mV) among all tested compounds, while showing the weakest EAG response to decane (EAG = 0.206 ± 0.008 mV).
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page (returned in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from whole docs tree except the d217 note listing the paper as unopened.

source.authors: Mengqing Zhou, Weicheng Yang, Gaoyin Wu, Xiaona Zhang, Fen Liu, Qi Sun, Xianyu Li, Jiya Wu, Tianyu Liang, Bibo Zhou
source.title: Antennal Responses and Odorant-Binding Protein 7 Binding of Rhoptroceros cyatheae (Selandriidae: Rhopographus) to Volatile Organic Compounds from Alsophila spinulosa

value: males gave stronger EAG responses than females to most of nine host-fern volatiles tested
method: electroantennography of adult sawflies, nine commercially available host volatiles in n-hexane at 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 uL/mL, 10 uL on a filter paper strip, n-hexane control first, concentrations from low to high with each applied once
conditions: adults and larvae field-collected in the Guizhou Chishui Alsophila National Nature Reserve, adults collected 1 to 3 days after emergence and reared separately to keep them virgin; 27 females and 27 males, each sample tested in triplicate; the nine tested compounds are a subset of 13 EAG-active GC-EAD compounds (the rest lacked pure commercial standards or were unstable); the Abstract says nine volatiles were identified as eliciting responses while Results section 2.1 says 13; sex differences were concentration-dependent and larger at high concentrations; 3-methylheptane gave slightly higher EAG in females but weak overall, and 3-methylheptane, tridecane, tetradecane and cedrene gave only weak responses in both sexes; antenna preparation not described; stimuli are nominal solution amounts
quote: For most volatile compounds, male sawflies exhibited stronger responses than females.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page. Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species and DOI absent from main (held lead from d217, p-xylene sentence now within the word limit but not needed). Name as printed in the title.

source.authors: Hua Xie, Hui Yuan, Yuyun Wang, Xinyu Tang, Meiru Yang, Li Zheng, Zongbo Li
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

value: phototaxis peaks: females at 360, 380 and 700 nm; males at 360 and 400 nm
method: three-chamber phototaxis apparatus with monochromator light from 300 to 700 nm in 20 nm steps, 10 min dark adaptation then 10 min exposure, beetles counted in each zone
conditions: adults collected alive from pine shoots in January to February at JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan; rearing and exact age not described ('newly emerged'); 30 same-sex adults per wavelength trial, three replicates, each beetle used once, per-sex numbers ambiguous; light intensity set by calibrating irradiance to 300 lux at the stationary zone, a photometric unit that is not photon-matched across wavelengths and not checked per wavelength; order of wavelengths not given; Results: both sexes showed significant phototaxis across all tested wavelengths (ANOVA females F(27,56) = 6.849, p < 0.001; males F(27,56) = 13.100, p < 0.001) and full light beat darkness (p < 0.001); the Discussion says most individuals stay in the stationary zone and a small portion disperse to the light or dark zone in nearly equal numbers; per-wavelength values are only in Figure 6
quote: Phototaxis tests revealed females are highly sensitive to 360 nm, 380 nm, and 700 nm wavelengths, while males exhibit high sensitivity to 360 nm and 400 nm.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI abstract (returned in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. The species is on main only for opsin_sequences_recovered, not behaviour_vision.

source.authors: Giovanni de Vincenzi, Primo Micarelli, Salvatore Viola, Gaspare Buffa, Virginia Sciacca, Vincenzo Maccarrone, Valentina Corrias, Francesca Romana Reinero, Cristina Giacoma, Francesco Filiciotto
source.title: Biological Sound vs. Anthropogenic Noise: Assessment of Behavioural Changes in Scyliorhinus canicula Exposed to Boats Noise

value: in an aquarium playback, sharks tended to occupy the least noisy sections
method: behavioural playback: individual sharks in an aquarium (4 x 1 x 1.5 m, divided into eight cells) exposed to four acoustic conditions (biological prey sounds, biological louder than boat noise, boat noise louder than biological, silent control), swimming time and cell use scored
conditions: twelve wild-caught specimens (six females, six males; trawled between Elba and Sardinia, held a month in an aquarium), each used in one trial, three replicates per condition, conditions in random sequence after 10 min habituation; biological tracks set 6 dB above or below boat noise within 100 to 140 dB re 1 uPa, levels measured with a hydrophone and processed in MATLAB; speaker has limited response below 200 Hz and particle motion was not reported; this is a behavioural response, not a hearing threshold; Results: swimming time rose most when boat noise exceeded biological sound (Kruskal-Wallis H = 39.4, N = 96, df = 3, p = 0.0005) and 'No significant differences were found among the other acoustic experimental conditions'; the paper also reports no difference in swimming time among cells, no up/down or left/right preference in the control, and a significant up/down difference (bottom use) in the two conditions where biological sound was louder or alone, with p = 0.05 counted as significant while the stated threshold is p < 0.05
quote: Moreover, their spatial distribution highlighted a tendency to occupy the least noisy sections of the aquarium.
note: Abstract sentence copied whole from the MDPI page. Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species on main for cff_hz, fovea, sense_electric only, not sense_hearing (whole-docs git grep).

source.authors: Raluca Ștefănescu, Constantin Roman, Liviu Dan Miron, Gheorghe Solcan, Vasile Vulpe, Luminița Diana Hrițcu, Mihai Musteata
source.title: Brainstem Auditory Evoked Potentials in Raccoon Dogs (Nyctereutes procynoides)

value: brainstem auditory evoked potential waves I, II, III and V identified
method: brainstem auditory evoked response with subdermal needle electrodes, 0.1 ms broadband clicks through foam earphones, 1000 stimuli averaged, contralateral ear masked with 50 dB SPL white noise
conditions: nine clinically healthy captive-bred adults (six males, three females, about 1 to 3 years) under xylazine and ketamine anaesthesia; a single click level of 90 dB SPL, so no hearing threshold or audiogram was measured; wave IV was treated as absent; mean latencies in ms (left, right, binaural): wave I 0.95, 1.00, 0.99; wave V 3.54, 3.61, 3.65; interpeak I-V 2.58, 2.60, 2.68; click repetition rate not reported; each examination repeated twice 5 min apart and averaged; the title prints the species as 'procynoides'
quote: Four waves (I, II, III and V) were identified and evaluated for latencies, morphologically similarity to those previously reported for other species (dogs, horses, cats, and ferret).
note: Abstract sentence copied whole (wording 'morphologically similarity' as printed). Licence: page prints the MDPI CC BY statement, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species on main for vision traits only, no sense_hearing (whole-docs git grep).

source.authors: Mechtilda Byamungu, Tusevo Zacarie, Alexis Makumyaviri M'Pondi, Philémon Mansinsa Diabakana, Andrew McMullin, Thomas Kröber, Steve Mihok, Patrick M. Guerin
source.title: Standardising visual control devices for Tsetse: East and Central African Savannah species Glossina swynnertoni, Glossina morsitans centralis and Glossina pallidipes

value: landings on 0.5 m2 blue-black oblong targets not significantly lower than on 1 m2 square targets
method: field trial of sticky-film targets: flies landing on blue-black targets of different size and shape counted, Latin square of days, sites and treatments
conditions: Serengeti (Death Valley near Seronera), Tanzania, July 2013, wild populations; three simultaneous replicates in the unbaited trials, flies counted by sex (sex-specific tables are supplementary); 1 m2 and 0.5 m2 square and oblong targets in blue-black and all-blue; the paper reports reflectance measured for the blue and black fabrics with a blue peak near 460 nm; devices were compared with one another and no blank control is described for the main comparison; this is a statement of no significant difference between sizes, not a spectral or acuity measurement; the Abstract also says blue-black 0.5 m2 targets performed better than all-blue equivalents for G. swynnertoni and G. m. centralis 'although not consistently', and that horizontal edge length correlated closely with landing rate (both taxa pooled in that sentence)
quote: Landings by G. swynnertoni on 0.5 m2 blue-black oblong targets were likewise not significantly lower than on equivalent 1 m2 square targets.
note: Abstract sentence copied whole from the PLOS page (returned in fragments). Licence: page states open access under the Creative Commons Attribution License and Crossref gives CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from the whole docs tree (git grep 'swynnertoni' and the DOI both empty). The sibling taxon G. m. centralis is a subspecies and is not filed.

source.authors: Andrea Gazzola, Bianca Guadin, Alessandro Balestrieri, Daniele Pellitteri-Rosa
source.title: Multimodal Cues Do Not Improve Predator Recognition in Green Toad Tadpoles

value: tadpole activity strongly decreased after chemical predator cues alone or combined with visual cues
method: individual tadpoles videorecorded before and after release of odour from tadpole-fed dragonfly larvae (Aeshna cyanea) into the arena; activity scored as the proportion of frames active
conditions: egg strings collected in May 2020 from canals east of Milan, Italy, hatched and reared in the laboratory with no predator experience, tested at Gosner stages 29 to 33 and chosen for similar size; 96 tadpoles, 24 per treatment (chemical, visual, combined, no-cue control), each tested alone and randomly assigned; 5 min acclimation, 20 min before and 20 min after the stimulus, five-second frames scored; predator cue was an Aeshna cyanea larva in a transparent container (visual) and 8 mL of pooled water from tadpole-fed larvae diluted 1:125 (chemical), with an empty container and plain water as controls; predators reused 2 to 3 times; generalised linear mixed models with trial as random effect; treatment effect on activity chi2 = 98.23, df = 3, p < 0.0001; visual cues alone did not change activity relative to controls; the odour stimulus is diet-conditioned larval water so the active compound is unknown
quote: The tadpole level of activity strongly decreased after exposure to either chemical cues alone or in combination with visual cues, while visual cues alone apparently did not elicit any defensive response.
note: Abstract sentence copied whole from the MDPI page (returned in fragments). Licence: page prints the MDPI CC BY statement, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from the whole docs tree (git grep 'balearicus' empty). Name as printed (title says green toad).

source.authors: Andrea Gazzola, Bianca Guadin, Alessandro Balestrieri, Daniele Pellitteri-Rosa
source.title: Multimodal Cues Do Not Improve Predator Recognition in Green Toad Tadpoles

value: tadpole position in the arena not affected by the visual presence of a caged dragonfly larva
method: individual tadpoles videorecorded with a predator (Aeshna cyanea larva) in a transparent container as the only cue; position scored as the proportion of frames spent on the side away from the container
conditions: egg strings collected in May 2020 from canals east of Milan, Italy, hatched and reared in the laboratory with no predator experience, tested at Gosner stages 29 to 33 and chosen for similar size; 96 tadpoles, 24 per treatment (chemical, visual, combined, no-cue control), each tested alone and randomly assigned; 5 min acclimation, 20 min before and 20 min after the stimulus, five-second frames scored; predator cue was an Aeshna cyanea larva in a transparent container (visual) and 8 mL of pooled water from tadpole-fed larvae diluted 1:125 (chemical), with an empty container and plain water as controls; predators reused 2 to 3 times; generalised linear mixed models with trial as random effect; visual cue treatment did not affect position (chi2 = 0.41, df = 1, p = 0.51); tadpole activity did not differ from controls with visual cues alone; tadpoles tended to spend more time on the container side across treatments; this is a null result for one predator species at a single distance and does not measure visual ability
quote: The position of tadpoles inside the arena was not affected by visual cues, suggesting that green toad tadpoles mainly rely on olfactory cues to assess the level of predation risk.
note: Abstract sentence copied whole from the MDPI page. Same licence and verification as the sense_chemical record from this paper. Filed as a null for the visual-only arm.
